meta.title: Four Short Texts and Their Parts
meta.textType: parts of a note, a caption, a blog post, and instructions

paragraphs: Four Short Texts and Their Parts, posted by Lily. This week, the Explorers learned about the parts of short texts. Every text has parts, and each part has a job. Parts help us read fast, and they help us write well. Our topic was Fruit Day, so all four texts are about fruit. I will describe each text, and I will name its parts.

First, here is a note from Teacher Kim. She wrote it on the board before the lesson. The greeting says, "Dear Explorers." The message says, "Please bring a variety of fresh fruit on Thursday." The closing says, "Thank you, Teacher Kim." A note has a greeting, a message, and a closing. It is short, because a person must understand it fast.

Second, here is a caption for a photo. Mia took the photo at the market, and it shows a table with red, yellow, and green fruit. Her caption says, "Many kinds of fruit at the market." The photo is bright, and the fruit looks fresh. A caption is one short line under a photo. It describes what you see, and it has only a few words.

Third, here is a short blog post by Leo. The title is "Why I Like Fruit," and the writer is Leo. Leo wrote it in ten minutes, and Teacher Kim read it first. The middle part says, "I think fresh fruit is better than candy." It also says, "Nobody at my table wanted candy after Fruit Day." The last line is a question, "What is your favorite fruit?" A blog post has a title, a writer, a middle part, and a last line. The post shows the point of view of the writer.

Last, here are the instructions for a Fruit Day poster. The title says, "How to Print a Poster." Step one says, "Open the file on the laptop." Step two says, "Check the level of paper in the printer." Step three says, "Click print." Step four says, "Take the page and put it on the wall." Instructions have a title and steps in order, and each step is short. We printed twenty posters, and we put them in the hall.
Now you can find the parts of every short text. Look at the next note or caption that you see, and name its parts. Which text do you like best?
text.summary: Lily shows four short texts for Fruit Day: a note, a caption, a blog post, and a set of instructions. She names the parts of each one, and the blog post gives the opinion of Leo.
